Worm's-eye ink painting under one enormous sacred birch whose trunk is a single hard black vertical stroke dividing the frame, roots spreading into bare paper mist. UNGNYEO, the bear-born woman, kneels at the foot of the birch in a simple white robe, holding a NEWBORN swaddled in white with a band of the ONE translucent warm tan #b8956a wash on the swaddle's edge — the only colour in the frame. HWANUNG, son of heaven, bends over her from the right, long hair and robes in sweeping calligraphic strokes, one hand on the birch. Behind Ungnyeo, a vast faint shape of a great bear is suggested only by a few wet dark ink masses, her first form. Topknots, no brimmed hats. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = ungnyeo, SECOND face = hwanung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.
